set.body:
Delivered: TidyResult, ContrastCsv, TemporalContrastCsv, score-component columns, workflow CSV and versioned scientific result archives; existing quoting, failure/provenance and base-R study-consumption evidence must be reused. io-export was absorbed here; no Arrow IPC implementation/dependency is currently present.

1. Freeze a finite result-family/export schema matrix at the reviewed candidate: scalar and named structured pair scores, endpoint reductions/contrasts, repetition edges, temporal point samples/bins, template predictions and OLS coefficients/diagnostics. State what lives in rows versus a linked versioned metadata sidecar; avoid an unfinishable 'every future result' promise. Scientific method implementation belongs to its own ticket.
2. Every admitted result variant retains typed key rendering/schema, source/method/parameter/plan identity, units/sign meaning, seed/selection when relevant, selected/successful/contributing denominators, explicit failures/exclusions and provenance. Structured components have stable names/order/units. Test commas/quotes/newlines/Unicode, empty outputs, exact 64-bit times/counts, missing values and nonfinite refusal; no NaN sentinel for typed failure or silent dropped rows.
3. Emit actual public artifacts in compiled examples and consume them independently in base R offline: compare row identities, exact counts and expected numeric values, not just successful read.csv. Normal workflows and routine JVM/JS tests remain R-free. New template, repetition and temporal result exports are integrated when those families land; they are whole-ticket completion dependencies, not reasons to defer the schema/scalar slice.
4. Resolve the retained io-export residual explicitly: implement optional Arrow IPC only in io's JVM source set, with schema/nullability/units/dictionary/time-width equivalence to the same canonical rows, independent readback and resource-close tests. No Arrow dependency in shared/JS or pure modules. It is optional for consumers but remains required ticket scope unless an explicit owner decision moves it; CSV completion alone cannot silently close it.

Exit: finite matrix fully covered by exported artifacts and schema/consumption tests; guides require no bespoke in-process result bridges. JSON archives continue under their existing codecs rather than a second persistence format.
Evidence gate: use the revision and backend locks in tools/r-parity/baseline.json and r-lock.json; new inputs/manifests are per-ticket, never edits to frozen baseline-cases.json. Record actual exported reference calls, independent analytic expectations, named numerical tolerances and exact identities. Normal workflows/tests require no R; R is an offline fixture oracle only. Exercise public JVM/Scala.js routes, typed failures and declared divergences; keep every failed/missing case. A function name or internal unit test is not cross-library conformance. New published laws require killed mutants. Update case evidence and PARITY.md only after measurement. See docs/TRACKER_REVIEW_2026-09-19.md for shared ownership and closure ordering.
set.title: Complete reusable baseline result exports
